accepted.question_text: Let T_b(A) denote a paracommutator determined by a Fourier kernel A and symbol b. Develop a general theory for vector-valued or operator-valued paracommutators analogous to the scalar theory, including criteria that characterize boundedness, compactness, and membership in Schatten-von Neumann classes for these vector or operator versions.

evidence.quote: Remark. It is also of interest to consider vector or operator versions of paracommutators. For instance, “big” Hankel operators in the sense of Axler [A] can in principle at least be reduced to suitable vectorial paracommutators. But, as far as we know, no general theory has yet been worked out in this case.

accepted.question_text: In the decomposition of a Hilbert-Schmidt operator T on L^2(R) into a sum of paracommutators obtained by first choosing an orthonormal basis {a_i} in L^2(R,dt) and expanding the Fourier kernel A(xi_1,xi_2) as a sum of terms involving that basis, can one choose the basis {a_i} in a canonical way rather than making an arbitrary orthonormal-basis choice?

evidence.quote: Let {a_i} be a fixed orthonormal basis in the Hilbert space L^2(R,dt). Then A clearly comes as a sum ... That is, T comes as a sum of paracommutators ... Is it possible to choose the basis {a_i} in some canonical way?

accepted.question_text: Extend the Euclidean theory of paracommutators from R^n to stratified groups G, such as the Heisenberg group. In particular, for kernels K that are homogeneous of degree -2Q on G x G and paracommutators T_b = T_b(K) defined from left translations and dilations, determine explicit hypotheses on K and the correct Besov-type spaces for b under which one obtains a full analogue of the Section 1 theory, including Schatten-class criteria beyond the p = 2 case and the needed minimality and maximality properties of the underlying function spaces.

evidence.quote: In this case we can no longer make use of the Fourier transform or at least it is less suitable here. However, we conjecture that most of the previous theory (see Section 1) carries over to the present situation.

To proceed further we need also the minimality of the space B^0_1 or, what is the same, the maximality of dually related spaces. It is also clear that the assumptions on K are less explicit than in the case of R^n, in which case they were formulated in terms of A (see Section 1). We therefore postpone a further treatment to a future occasion.

accepted.question_text: For compact trilinear forms on three Hilbert spaces, define multilinear analogues S_p of the Schatten-von Neumann classes for 1 < p < 2 and 2 < p < infinity by interpolation between the nuclear class S_1, the Hilbert-Schmidt class S_2, and the compact class S_infinity. Do the real and complex interpolation definitions of S_p coincide, do they agree with the separately defined class S_2, and is the whole scale S_p for 0 < p <= infinity closed under interpolation?

evidence.quote: What about S_p, 1 < p < 2 or 2 < p < oo? We suggest defining S_p by interpolation, either real or complex, i.e. S_p=(S_1,S_oo)_{theta,p} or S_p=[S_1,S_oo]_theta where 1/p=1-theta. It is not clear that two definitions coincide, as in the operator case, nor that they agree with the definition of S_2.
Also, it is not clear at all that the entire scale S_p, 0 < p <= oo, is closed for interpolation.

accepted.question_text: Let S_p denote the trilinear-form classes defined by the first method, and let S~_p denote the classes defined by approximation numbers s_n(B), namely by requiring the sequence {s_n(B)} to lie in l^p. For compact trilinear forms on Hilbert spaces, is it true that S_p = S~_p for 0 < p <= infinity?
accepted.context_brief: Equivalence of two multilinear Schatten scales

evidence.quote: But is it true that S_p = S~_p?

accepted.question_text: For the approximation-number-based classes S~_p of compact trilinear forms on Hilbert spaces, determine whether S~_p is a Banach space for finite p.

evidence.quote: It is not even clear that the spaces S~_p are Banach spaces for any p < oo.
